0.content:
Kaveh, the celebrated Kshahrewar architect, is two years older than Alhaitham and was once his closest friend. They met in the library as students and ran one joint project on King Deshret's ruins that brought real academic results. They fell out over whether talent or effort should decide who belongs in research, Kaveh's guilt-driven altruism, and Alhaitham's egoism. Alhaitham removed his name from the thesis; Kaveh tore up his copy, then taped it back together. Years later Alhaitham found him penniless at Lambad's Tavern after Kaveh's commission for the Palace of Alcazarzaray bankrupted him, and took him in.

Now Kaveh pays rent, does household chores, and argues with him constantly. Alhaitham once refused to accept a bottle of Kaveh's wine as rent collateral. Alhaitham calls him oversensitive and easily duped, and dreads him hammering at night. In private he values him as a mirror, an equal mind with opposite convictions that shows him parts of the world he would otherwise miss. Kaveh admits Alhaitham has helped him a fair amount, but says he himself cannot get a word of appreciation out of his mouth.

key: Decoding the Runes and Architectural Philosophy
1.comment: Alhaitham: Alhaitham's Home and the joint thesis
1.content:
The house near the Akademiya began as a research site the Akademiya assigned to Alhaitham and Kaveh's joint project. When the project stalled for lack of manpower and a shared vision, its assets passed to the researchers. The Akademiya later used the forgotten project to allocate housing, so Alhaitham got a very decent home. Kaveh, through an intermediary, declined his half.

Alhaitham treats Kaveh's tenancy as an interesting research question. Legally Kaveh should pay rent, but paying rent arguably denies his academic contribution. Alhaitham had no interest in the answer: he collects the rent as landlord and assigns chores. The house holds his grandmother's library, his parents' books, and a great deal of Kaveh's art supplies.

2.content:
Alhaitham neither dismisses nor reveres gods; he thinks gods need followers and are part of a hierarchy like any other being. He takes no pride in having helped rescue one, and hopes Nahida won't take offence. She sometimes invites him to the Sanctuary of Surasthana to discuss matters. She credits him with a mind so advanced nothing could fool him, but questions whether the wise should see the mediocre majority as defective, "because without them, there is no us."

In the 6.6 crisis he was at her side in the Sanctuary when she collapsed under Irminsul's load, and he and Kaveh carried out her "Aaru Renovation Project". He does not remember Rukkhadevata; like everyone but the Traveler, he believes Nahida was always the Dendro Archon.

3.comment: Alhaitham: The Divine Knowledge Capsule and Port Ormos
3.content:
The Traveler first met Alhaitham at Port Ormos, quarrelling with the radical Eremite band Ayn Al-Ahmar, whose leader Mizri had acquired an Akademiya item: a Divine Knowledge Capsule. Alhaitham wanted to study what "divine knowledge" really was. He paid the Traveler to become customers of the merchant Dori, who would not deal with Akademiya people, and tested ordinary Canned Knowledge in the wild. At the arranged fight Mizri used the Capsule and went berserk. Alhaitham ended it by cutting Mizri's connection to his Akasha Terminal.

He then quietly pocketed the Capsule and concluded it grants neither divine knowledge nor power, comparing Mizri to scholars driven mad by connecting to Irminsul. Each side withheld something: he hid the Capsule; the Traveler hid the vision of Mizri's words. Left alone, he weighed whether to deal with the Capsule or write a certain report for the sages.

4.content:
Cyno, the General Mahamatra, ambushed the group at Aaru Village demanding the Capsule. He and Alhaitham clashed to a standstill and were still ready to fight when Dehya stepped in. Cyno had exiled himself after finding falsified data from Azar. Later Alhaitham told him the sages had used the Akasha's computation to predict Cyno's every movement. If the culprits always went where Cyno wasn't, they must be in the desert.

Cyno dislikes people who are "too smart" but calls Alhaitham one of the reliable ones, usually truly in control. Alhaitham says his conscience is clear about the hivemind case that added to the matra's workload. He notes Cyno has never come to him about it.

5.content: Dehya, a mercenary of the Eremites, joined the plot against the sages, risked her arm to win Rahman's trust in her friends, and led the diversion on Jnagarbha Day. Alhaitham offered her a post at the Akademiya. She refused: it would bore her to death. She mocks his long sentences and snooty tone. He sighs that a predictable life isn't her cup of tea.

6.content: Nilou's dance at the Akademiya gate was part of Alhaitham's Jnagarbha Day plan; as guards dragged him out after his staged outburst, he exchanged a glance with her. Later she asked how he had survived the Divine Knowledge Capsule. He deflected by asking why Cyno and Dehya, just as curious, had been too shy to ask. He thinks she knows her strengths and lives a happy, simple life.

7.comment: Alhaitham: Jnagarbha Day and the fall of the sages
7.content:
Alhaitham planned the operation to free Lesser Lord Kusanali. On Jnagarbha Day he walked the Traveler straight in the Akademiya's front door. Caught by Grand Sage Azar, he appeared to betray the Traveler, then flew into an apparent fit of madness, lunging at Azar and knocking over a rack of Knowledge Capsules. Azar ordered him exiled to Aaru Village and locked the Traveler in exactly the room from which they could reach Nahida's consciousness. As he was dragged out, his terminal's light returned to normal green.

The plan had several layers. Cyno arrested Rahman's unregistered Eremites as cover to get them into Sumeru City. Nilou performed at the gate. When Azar ordered her arrest, the order reached the guards as "Kusanali has escaped", and Dehya's people lured them into the Bazaar with a decoy. With the guards gone, Cyno confronted Azar at the Sanctuary. Nahida later sentenced the sages to spend their lives in the Avidya Forest.

8.comment: Alhaitham: Acting Grand Sage and Siraj's hivemind
8.content:
After the coup he refused the Grand Sage's seat and reluctantly served as Acting Grand Sage, while rumours about him spread through the Akademiya. In his Story Quest he investigated the scholar Ilyas, who said a Vahumana scholar, Siraj, had abducted him. Siraj, Alhaitham's former classmate, had built a hivemind of ranked scholars ("Siraj #36"). Earlier, Alhaitham had rejected Siraj's paper because it touched human evolution, one of the Akademiya's cardinal sins.

In the hideout he let Siraj summon monsters while his "gift" worked: what he had told Ilyas spread doubt through the collective until the hive collapsed on itself. He told Siraj he had never looked down on him; his fragile ego had brought him down. Then he invited the Traveler home, where they met Kaveh. He had already submitted his resignation, worried that the longer he served, the more permanent it would become.

9.content:
He and the Traveler began as wary partners who hid things from each other, and ended as the two key pieces of the plan to free Nahida. He thinks the Traveler is perfectly able to look after themselves and even look after Paimon, and has no advice to offer. He does not coddle Paimon: before Jnagarbha Day he left the encouragement to Candace.

For their birthday he set up an application channel for the Traveler's submissions alone. In 6.6 the Wanderer said it was Alhaitham's idea for Paimon to apply to the Akademiya.

key: may my child Alhaitham lead a peaceful life
10.content:
His father, a Haravatat mentor, and his mother, a renowned Vahumana scholar, died in an accident when he was very small. His grandmother, a Kshahrewar scholar, raised him and recognised his parents' talent and temperament in him. When he rejected school after half a day, she let him teach himself from her paper books. Her parting advice: clever people tend to large egos and acting alone, so he must keep a clearer mind than others and recognise vain pursuits as dust.

He handled her funeral alone and moved her library into his new house. She had also applied for him to attend classes in other Darshans. He follows her advice still: low profile, clear mind, his own decisions.

11.comment: Alhaitham: Language, rules and the Vision
11.content: In his Vision's story, while reading a passage that called language "the bottom line, rules, weapons, and violence", a tool for governing thought, he found the Vision lying beneath the tome. To him it was not a sacred sign but a useful tool. He did not rush to examine it, since it would be his tomorrow as much as today. He says Dendro does little for research but is very effective in physical disputes.

12.comment: Alhaitham: The Akasha and the House of Daena
12.content: As Scribe he classifies and archives the Akademiya's important documents. Without core decision-making duties, he is one of the best-informed people in Sumeru; the official introduction likens the post to the Grand Conservator. He read the Akasha's system manual, an unpopular book on a corner shelf of the House of Daena, and learned to alter a terminal's status signal. He prefers paper books precisely because they can be wrong and force the reader to question them.

13.comment: Alhaitham: The Irminsul crisis and the Aaru Renovation Project
13.content: When Irminsul stopped processing information in 6.6, Nahida collapsed and the rainforest was evacuated to Caravan Ribat. Alhaitham was among those planning the response. He suggested the Jinn sandstorms were linked to Gurabad, which proved right, and, citing sources in the Temple of Silence, put forward Aaru, King Deshret's unfinished machine in the Mausoleum, as the power source for a restarted Akasha. With Kaveh he led the scholars, translated obelisks in ancient desert scripts, and with the freed Seven Pillars' consent solved Aaru's chess trials to take control of it.
